title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 193 (Agent’s responsibility for sub-agent appointed without authority)

content.overview: Where an agent, without having authority to do so, has appointed a person to act as a sub-agent, the agent stands towards such person in the relation of a principal to an agent, and is responsible for his acts both to the principal and to third persons; the principal is not represented by or responsible for the acts of the person so employed, nor is that person responsible to the principal.
content.glance: Unauthorized sub-agent: original agent is principal to that person and responsible to principal and third persons; principal not represented by or responsible for the unauthorized appointee.
content.study: Where an agent, without having authority to do so, has appointed a person to act as a sub-agent, the agent stands towards such person in the relation of a principal to an agent, and is responsible for his acts both to the principal and to third persons; the principal is not represented by or responsible for the acts of the person so employed, nor is that person responsible to the principal. Contrast s. 192 (properly appointed sub-agent).

sections.heading: Appointment without authority
sections.body: Agent appoints a sub-agent without authority to do so.

sections.heading: Agent’s responsibility
sections.body: Agent stands as principal to that person and is responsible for his acts to the principal and third persons.

sections.heading: Principal not bound
sections.body: Principal is not represented by or responsible for the acts of the person so employed; that person is not responsible to the principal.

provisions.title: Agent’s responsibility for sub-agent appointed without authority

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 193 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Confirm lack of authority to appoint sub-agent; hold original agent responsible as principal to the appointee; exclude principal from representation and responsibility.

examTips: Unauthorized sub-agent falls on the appointing agent.
